title: BenchX identity policy
description: A project's standing experiment definition (docs/design/benchmark-result-schema.md section 4.3): which reported facts results must share to be points of one series, how values are normalized before matching, and optional conditions on sibling measurements. The server applies it to stored results; producers never send it. Placement in the result records what a fact is; this document decides what role it plays.
$comment: Draft. Rules the schema cannot express and the server enforces: a path is a JSON Pointer into the reported coordinates (the result's project, source, benchmark, and coordinates members, never revision, measurement, procedure, or provenance); the most specific scope wins, and among rules of equal specificity the later one wins; within one rule the longest matching path wins, so a role on a subtree can be overridden for one of its members; a null fact never equals anything, including another null; changing anything here other than description requires a new identity_schema. Comparison profiles (section 5.5) are one-off experiment definitions over a run and are not expressed in this document.

identity_schema.description: Versioned name of the projection. Enters comparison_fingerprint, so series built under different schemas never mix.

default.description: Role of every reported fact no rule names.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the reported coordinates, such as /coordinates/environment/facts/os/kernel.

scope.description: Which results a rule applies to. Every member present must match; an empty scope is project-wide. Specificity is the number of members present.

workload.description: Workload name, or a glob over it.

oneOf.description: match: equal values are required to share a series. ignore: the fact is kept on the result and shown beside the series, but does not split it.
Keep the first depth dot-separated components of a version string: 2.39.1 at depth 2 is 2.39.
Replace values by an explicit table, such as benchmark revisions to declared versions. A value absent from the table is kept as is.
Canonicalize a source URI (scheme, host case, trailing .git).

condition.description: Restricts a series to results whose sibling measurement (same attempt_key) satisfies a bound, such as zero throttle events. A condition on a state that the workload itself influences selects on a consequence of the thing measured and can bias the series; section 4.3 discusses this.

estimator.description: Estimator applied to the sibling's observations, by name.

missing.description: What happens when the sibling is absent or not success: exclude the result from the series, or keep it.
